articles.title: M62 Eastbound Closed Near Rochdale, Motorists Warned of Delays
articles.excerpt: Motorists are advised to expect delays on the M62 eastbound near Rochdale due to a closure beyond Junction 21 on Wednesday evening, 21 October 2026.
articles.content_html:
Motorists travelling on the M62 eastbound near Rochdale are being warned of significant delays following a closure beyond Junction 21 on Wednesday evening, 21 October 2026.

The closure has been reported due to unspecified circumstances, and drivers are advised to approach the area with caution. Traffic alerts indicate that those heading towards West Yorkshire should prepare for potential disruptions.

Authorities have not yet provided an estimated time for the reopening of the motorway, and further updates are expected as the situation develops.

Motorists are encouraged to check traffic updates and plan alternative routes if necessary to avoid delays.

articles.content_html:

No waiting or loading will be permitted at any time along the affected roads. Specific details regarding the roads impacted will be provided in the council's official notice.

Residents and visitors are advised to plan their journeys in advance, as there will be no alternative routes available for vehicles during this period.

For further information and to view a map of the roadworks and restrictions across Greater Manchester, residents can visit the council's website.

articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that Fielding Street in Middleton will be temporarily closed for roadworks starting on 3 November 2026, affecting local traffic.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that part of Fielding Street in Middleton will be temporarily closed from 3 November 2026. The closure will extend from the junction with Clough Road and will continue 35 metres down the road in a south-westerly direction.

During this period, there will be no alternative route available for vehicles, which may cause disruptions for local traffic. Residents and motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and seek alternative routes where possible.

The roadworks are part of ongoing infrastructure improvements in the area, aimed at enhancing road safety and traffic flow. Further details regarding the duration of the works and any additional restrictions will be communicated by the council as the start date approaches.

For more information on this and other roadworks in the area, residents can visit the Rochdale Borough Council website, where they can also view a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester.

articles.title: Power Outage in Newhey Linked to 'Third-Party Interference'
articles.excerpt: Residents in Newhey experienced a power outage lasting approximately three hours following a loud bang linked to third-party interference on the electricity network.
articles.content_html:
Residents in Newhey, Rochdale, were left without power for around three hours following a loud bang associated with an incident on the electricity network. The disruption occurred on the evening of October 18, 2026, and was reported by Electricity North West, who stated that the outage was due to 'third-party interference' on their high-voltage network.

According to a message from Electricity North West, the loud bang was heard at a property on Ogden Lane at the same time the power interruption occurred. While most residents had their power restored by 23:17, one customer remained without supply as further investigations were conducted to ensure safety before restoration could take place.

Electricity North West expressed appreciation for the patience and understanding of the affected residents during the investigation. They confirmed that their teams were working to identify the root cause of the fault and ensure the safety of the network before restoring power to the remaining customer.

Residents are encouraged to stay updated through official channels for any further developments regarding the power supply in their area. For those affected, it is recommended to check the Electricity North West website or contact their customer service for assistance.

articles.title: Temporary Closure of Hillcrest Road in Rochdale for Roadworks from 26 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Temporary closure of Hillcrest Road will take place from 26 October to 30 October 2026, affecting local traffic and access.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that Hillcrest Road will be temporarily closed for roadworks from 12 midnight on Monday, 26 October 2026, until 11.59pm on Friday, 30 October 2026. The closure will affect a section of the road, specifically from a point 57 metres east of its junction with Queensway for a distance of 20 metres heading east.

During this period, motorists will need to use alternative routes. The suggested diversion will take drivers along Queensway, Albion Street, and Newchurch Street to navigate around the closure.

This roadworks initiative is part of ongoing efforts by the council to improve local infrastructure and ensure safer travel for residents and visitors. The exact nature of the works has not been detailed in the announcement, but such projects typically involve repairs or upgrades to the road surface and associated facilities.

Local residents and commuters are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and allow for extra travel time during the roadworks. Further updates may be provided as the work progresses, and residents can check the council's website for additional information and maps of the affected areas.

articles.title: Spudbros Opens New Location at EG Station on Manchester Road in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Jacket potato fans in Rochdale welcomed the opening of Spudbros at EG Station on Manchester Road, with the first 100 customers receiving a free meal.
articles.content_html:
Spudbros, a popular jacket potato brand from Preston, has officially opened its new location at the EG Station on Manchester Road in Rochdale. The opening attracted large crowds, with many eager customers queuing for the chance to try the viral spud offerings.

The first 100 customers through the doors received a free meal, further adding to the excitement of the launch. This new outlet is expected to bring a fresh dining option to the area, catering to both locals and visitors alike.

Spudbros is known for its variety of toppings and quick service, making it a popular choice for those looking for a quick bite. The opening at EG Station marks a significant expansion for the brand, which has gained a loyal following since its inception.

Local residents can now enjoy the convenience of having Spudbros nearby, potentially boosting foot traffic in the area. The new location is likely to become a go-to spot for jacket potato enthusiasts in Rochdale.

articles.title: Bus Services Suspended Between Rochdale Town Centre and Freehold Following Collision
articles.excerpt: A road traffic collision at Westwood has led to the suspension of bus services between Rochdale Town Centre and Freehold, with ticket acceptance in place on multiple routes.
articles.content_html:
A road traffic collision at Westwood has resulted in the suspension of bus services between Rochdale Town Centre and Freehold. The incident has disrupted travel for many commuters.

In response to the disruption, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has implemented ticket acceptance on several bus services. Affected routes include the 17, 57, 59, 76, 76A, 81, 83, 84, 114, 149, 181, 182, 409, 411, 435, 436, and 471.

Passengers are advised to check the TfGM travel alerts page for updates on the situation and any changes to service availability. The collision has caused significant delays, and it is currently unclear when normal service will resume.

Local residents and commuters may experience longer journey times due to the disruption. TfGM is working to resolve the situation as quickly as possible.

articles.title: Temporary Road Closures on Trafalgar Street and Joy Street in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced roadworks on Nowell Road and Pershore Road in Middleton, set to begin on 26 October 2026, which will temporarily close sections of these roads.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that roadworks will commence on Nowell Road and Pershore Road in Middleton on 26 October 2026. The works are part of ongoing infrastructure improvements aimed at enhancing road safety and traffic flow.

During the roadworks, sections of both Nowell Road and Pershore Road will be temporarily closed. Specific details regarding the closures have yet to be fully outlined, but motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and seek alternative routes where possible.

In addition to the works on Nowell Road and Pershore Road, roadworks will also take place on Thornham Lane from 26 October 2026, with closures expected from 9am to 4pm each day until 30 October 2026. The closure will affect part of Thornham Lane starting at the junction with Rochdale Road, extending 23 metres in an easterly direction. Access for emergency vehicles will be maintained where safe to do so.

Furthermore, roadworks will begin on Wallhead Road from midnight on 27 October 2026 until 6am on 28 October 2026, with part of Wallhead Street closed from the junction with Wallhead Road extending 50 metres south. There will be no alternative route for vehicles during this time, but emergency vehicle access will be preserved. Lastly, Halifax Road in Hurstead will also undergo roadworks from midnight on 26 October 2026 until 11.59pm on 1 November 2026, which may affect local traffic patterns.

articles.title: Overnight Road Closures Planned at Sudden Junction, Rochdale from October 12 to 15
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council will implement overnight road closures around Sudden Junction from October 12 to 15 for resurfacing work, affecting traffic routes and diversions.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that overnight road closures will take place around Sudden Junction from Monday, October 12, to Thursday, October 15. The closures are necessary for resurfacing work, which will include refreshing road markings and renewing traffic signs.

The affected roads will be closed nightly between 8pm and 5am. Manchester Road in Castleton will be closed northbound between Onslow Street and Bolton Road, impacting traffic heading towards Rochdale town centre. Additionally, Silk Street will operate as one-way towards Tesco, preventing drivers from travelling from Tesco towards Manchester Road. Traffic on Bolton Road will also be restricted from turning right onto Manchester Road towards Castleton.

In a statement, the council confirmed that fully signed diversion routes will be in place to guide motorists during the closures. The resurfacing work aims to improve road safety and traffic flow in the area, which has seen increased usage in recent months.

Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and allow extra time for travel during the closure period. The council will continue to provide updates as the work progresses.

articles.title: Roadworks Scheduled on Well i' th' Lane in Rochdale from 24 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced roadworks on Well i' th' Lane starting 24 October 2026, with alternative routes provided for motorists.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks will commence on Well i' th' Lane from 12 midnight on Saturday, 24 October 2026, continuing until 11.59pm on Sunday, 1 November 2026. During this period, part of the road will be temporarily closed to facilitate the necessary works.

Motorists travelling southbound will be diverted via Queen Victoria Street, Oldham Road, and Queensway. The council advises drivers to plan their journeys accordingly to avoid delays during the roadworks.

In addition to Well i' th' Lane, several other roads in the Rochdale area will also undergo maintenance. Notably, Willbutts Lane and Rooley Street will see roadworks starting on 12 October 2026, with closures expected to last for a maximum of 21 days. Willbutts Lane will be closed at the junction with Edenfield Road, extending 14 metres westward, while Rooley Street will be closed at the same junction, extending 10 metres eastward.

Egerton Street in Heywood will also be closed from 12 midnight on Tuesday, 20 October 2026, until 11.59pm on Sunday, 1 November 2026, with the closure beginning at the junction with Hind Hill Street and extending 165 metres westward. Residents and commuters are encouraged to check the Rochdale Borough Council's website for further details, including maps of the affected areas and updates on the roadworks.

articles.title: Castleton night works: Manchester Road’s three traffic phases
articles.excerpt: Overnight restrictions run until 8 November. The council has not published dates for individual phases.
articles.content_html:
Manchester Road drivers face overnight restrictions for Bee Network Phase 2 resurfacing, scheduled from 12 October to 8 November 2026, 8pm–5am. Only one phase operates at a time.

Phase 1 closes Manchester Road between Onslow Street and Bolton Road. Silk Street is westbound-only from Tesco to Manchester Road; right turns from Bolton Road onto Manchester Road are banned.

Phase 2 bans north-eastbound travel on Manchester Road from Bolton Road to Roch Valley Way. There is no left turn from Bolton Road onto Manchester Road. The old Manchester Road section must exit via Roch Valley Way. Manchester Road traffic can only turn left onto Bolton Road. Westbound travel on Silk Street from Tesco to Manchester Road is prohibited.

Phase 3 bans south-westbound travel between Roch Valley Way and Bolton Road. There is no left turn from Edinburgh Way onto Manchester Road, or right turn from Roch Valley Way. Silk Street closes between Manchester Road and Tesco, with no right turn into it from Manchester Road.

Diversions will be signed. Check the current phase before travelling: https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/directory-record/2618/various-roads-roadworks-in-rochdale-from-12-october-2026

articles.title: Heywood councillors vote to end Hopwood Triangle road closure trial
articles.excerpt: Heywood Township councillors have voted unanimously to end the Hopwood Triangle traffic trial after sustained opposition from residents, while the Coronation Avenue HGV parking restriction will remain.
articles.content_html:
Common sense has finally prevailed. At an extraordinary Heywood Township meeting last tonight, councillors voted UNANIMOUSLY to bring the Hopwood Triangle trial on Middleton Road and Magdala Street to an end and remove the road closures. The restriction preventing heavy wagons from parking on Coronation Avenue will remain in place, helping to protect local streets.

For residents, this decision has been a long time coming. The consultation results could hardly have been clearer: 86% of the approximately 700 respondents opposed the scheme. Yet despite that overwhelming response, the trial was approved and went ahead. Residents subsequently raised serious concerns about congestion, access, road safety and the effect on local businesses. People living on Manchester Road also felt they had been left out of the original consultation despite subsequently experiencing the impact of displaced traffic. The timing was another major concern. The trial began during the quieter summer holiday period, with residents warning that the true impact would become much more apparent once schools reopened and normal traffic levels returned. Last night, local people turned out in numbers to make sure their voices were heard. More than 50 residents attended the extraordinary meeting, but the size of the room at the old Police Station quickly became an issue. With residents understandably frustrated about access to a public meeting concerning their own streets, tensions rose and the meeting came close to being suspended. At that point, Reform UK Councillor Stuart Crawford intervened constructively. Recognising that many residents had already heard the Highways presentations and wanted councillors to make a decision, Stuart engaged directly with those in attendance, helped calm the situation and pressed for the meeting to move on to the vote rather than risk the evening ending without a decision. The vote was then taken. Every councillor voted to end the trial. That means the temporary road closures will now be removed, while the restriction on heavy wagons parking on Coronation Avenue will remain. And then there is the cost. The figures presented for the scheme are stark: £110,000 to install the temporary measures. That is £110,000 of public money associated with introducing and then removing a trial which had already been rejected by 86% of consultation respondents. The scheme was voted through back in November by Labour councillors Angela Brown, Paul O’Neil, Peter Hodgkinson, Peter Joinson, Susan Emmott and Liam O’Rourke, despite 86% of consultation respondents opposing it. Last night, the decision went the other way. Whatever political arguments follow, one fact should not be forgotten: local residents spoke up, kept speaking up and ultimately got the result they had been asking for. Reform UK will continue to stand with residents when decisions affecting their communities need to be challenged. A huge thank you to everybody who attended, everybody who responded to the original consultation, and everybody who refused to allow their concerns to be ignored. This was people power in action, and people power won.
articles.source_name: Reform UK statement supplied to Rochdale Daily

articles.title: Edenfield Road reopens early after resurfacing work completed ahead of schedule
articles.excerpt: Edenfield Road between the White Lion and Nutters has reopened early after contractors completed resurfacing and lining work ahead of schedule.
articles.content_html:
Edenfield Road between the White Lion and Nutters has reopened to traffic after resurfacing works were completed ahead of schedule.

Norden councillor Paul Ellison MBE confirmed on Saturday that the road is now open and that the road closure which had been expected on Sunday will no longer be required.

Contractors completed the main resurfacing work early, with Saturday seeing the final road-lining work carried out. Cat's-eye road studs are due to be fitted on Monday, but the road itself has reopened.

Councillor Ellison thanked Rochdale Borough Council, A&T Surfacing and Rhodes & Son Construction for completing the scheme ahead of schedule, describing the finished work as a fantastic job.

The reopening will be welcome news for residents and motorists using one of the principal routes through Norden. The works had required traffic restrictions while the carriageway was resurfaced, with further closure time originally expected over the weekend.

With the contractors finishing earlier than planned, drivers can now use the stretch between the White Lion and Nutters without the anticipated Sunday closure.

Motorists should remain aware that the final cat's-eye inserts are expected to be fitted on Monday and should follow any temporary traffic management in place while that work is completed.

articles.title: Loombrook Meadows: 302 new homes coming to Castleton - what we know so far
articles.excerpt: Barratt Homes has broken ground on a 302-home development at Cowm Top Lane, with two, three and four bedroom houses expected to go on sale from autumn. What's being built, who it's for, and the affordability question.
articles.content_html:
A brand new development of two, three and four bedroom homes is coming to Castleton - and buyers are already being invited to register their interest.

Loombrook Meadows, being built by Barratt Homes on Cowm Top Lane, will deliver 302 new homes on the southern edge of the borough. Construction began in early June, and the developer expects the first properties to be available to reserve from autumn 2026.

Barratt says the homes will be built with a stone effect intended to match the character of the local area, using modern construction methods designed to make them more energy efficient and cheaper to run. The development is expected to support around 604 jobs during construction.

The developer is pitching the site at young professionals, first-time buyers and growing families, pointing to Castleton railway station, the M62 and local schools and shops on the doorstep. Rhys Nicholson, managing director at Barratt Homes Manchester, said the scheme had already seen strong interest from those groups and encouraged anyone interested to register for updates on the homes available later this year.

How affordable will they be?

Prices for Loombrook Meadows have not yet been released. As a guide, Barratt's other current developments in the wider area list two to four bedroom homes from around £198,000 up to £459,000, and the company promotes schemes such as reduced-rate mortgage products and assisted moves for buyers with a home to sell. Until the first releases are priced, it is impossible to say where Loombrook Meadows will sit within that range, or how many of the 302 homes will be classed as affordable housing - a figure usually settled through the planning process. Rochdale Daily has asked for details of the affordable housing provision and will update this article when they are confirmed.

The bigger picture

The development lands in the middle of a familiar local argument. Rochdale, like most of Greater Manchester, does not have enough homes: demand for social housing far outstrips supply, private rents have climbed steeply, and many working households find themselves priced out of buying altogether. New building on this scale is one of the few levers that can ease that pressure.

At the same time, large housing schemes in and around Castleton routinely draw concern from existing residents about traffic on already busy roads, pressure on GP surgeries and school places, and the loss of open land. Those arguments were aired when the Cowm Top site went through planning, and they will not disappear now the diggers have arrived.

What is not in dispute is the need. A borough of around 220,000 people cannot house its next generation in its existing stock, and every credible plan for Rochdale's future involves building substantially more homes. The test for Loombrook Meadows will be whether the homes that emerge are ones ordinary Rochdale families can actually afford - and whether the infrastructure around them keeps pace.

Buyers can register their interest through the Barratt Homes website.

articles.title: Lives cut short: Remembering the young people lost on Rochdale's roads
articles.excerpt: A look at the tragic loss of young lives on Rochdale's roads since 2020 and the ongoing efforts to improve road safety across the borough.
articles.content_html:
Every fatal road traffic collision leaves behind grieving families, devastated friends and communities asking whether more could have been done to prevent another life being cut short.

Since 2020, a number of young people have tragically lost their lives on roads across Rochdale borough. While every collision has had its own unique circumstances, each has served as a stark reminder that road safety is not simply about statistics – it is about sons, daughters, brothers, sisters, classmates and friends whose futures were taken away far too soon.

One of the most heartbreaking incidents came in April 2025 when six-year-old Myra Tahseen died after being struck by a vehicle on Ashfield Road. Emergency services fought to save her, but she sadly died from her injuries. The tragedy prompted an outpouring of grief across Rochdale, with floral tributes left at the scene and specialist officers supporting her family while investigations continued.

Although fatalities involving children and young people are thankfully rare, they remain one of the leading causes of death for those aged between five and nineteen across the United Kingdom. Rochdale's own Joint Strategic Needs Assessment highlights that land transport collisions remain among the principal causes of death for young people and reports that the borough's rate of children killed or seriously injured on the roads is around 15 per 100,000 population.

Behind every fatal collision lies a complex combination of circumstances. Excessive speed, distraction, impairment through drink or drugs, failure to wear seatbelts, poor weather, inexperience and momentary lapses in concentration can all contribute to devastating outcomes. Road safety experts consistently stress that many serious collisions are preventable through safer driving behaviour.

Young drivers remain disproportionately represented in serious road collisions nationwide. Inexperience, overconfidence and risk-taking behaviour can all increase the likelihood of being involved in a collision, particularly during the first years after passing a driving test. Equally, young pedestrians and cyclists are among the most vulnerable road users, particularly near schools, residential estates and busy roads.

Greater Manchester Police's Serious Collision Investigation Unit continues to investigate every fatal collision thoroughly, examining witness statements, CCTV, vehicle data, road conditions and forensic evidence to establish exactly what happened. These investigations often continue for many months before an inquest is held, allowing families to receive answers and, where appropriate, criminal proceedings to take place.

Road safety is not solely the responsibility of drivers. Pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists and passengers all have a role to play in reducing risk. Simple decisions such as slowing down in residential areas, putting mobile phones away, wearing seatbelts correctly, using pedestrian crossings where available and remaining alert around schools can make a significant difference.

Across Rochdale borough, organisations continue to work together to improve road safety through engineering improvements, education campaigns, enforcement against dangerous driving and community awareness initiatives. Every serious collision provides lessons that can help prevent future tragedies.

For the families who have lost loved ones, however, those lessons come at an unimaginable cost. Birthdays go uncelebrated, empty seats remain at family tables and communities continue to remember young lives that ended far too soon.

The hope shared by police, road safety campaigners and residents alike is that by learning from these tragedies, encouraging responsible driving and remaining vigilant on every journey, fewer families will have to experience the heartbreak of losing someone they love on Rochdale's roads.

articles.title: Residents voice concerns over dangerous driving and alleged street racing on Milkstone Road
articles.excerpt: Residents have raised concerns about dangerous driving and alleged street racing on Milkstone Road, with calls for stronger enforcement to improve road safety.
articles.content_html:
Residents and business owners along Milkstone Road are continuing to raise concerns about dangerous driving, excessive speeding and alleged late-night street racing, with many calling for stronger enforcement before someone is seriously injured.

Milkstone Road is one of Rochdale's busiest routes, carrying thousands of vehicles each day while also serving local shops, schools, places of worship and residential streets. For many residents, the road should be a safe route for families, pedestrians and cyclists. However, some say that during evenings and late at night, it can become the scene of drivers accelerating aggressively, revving engines and travelling at excessive speeds.

While there is no evidence to suggest organised street racing is a regular occurrence, residents have reported vehicles appearing to race one another, performing rapid acceleration and driving in a manner they believe is dangerous. Such behaviour can create significant risks for other motorists, pedestrians and nearby residents, particularly on a road with numerous junctions, crossings and side streets.

The concerns reflect a wider national problem. Police forces across the country have stepped up action against illegal street racing and antisocial driving, warning that the behaviour can have devastating consequences. The Government has also strengthened powers allowing police to seize and destroy vehicles used in antisocial driving offences in appropriate circumstances.

Road safety already forms one of the priorities for Greater Manchester Police's Milkstone and Deeplish neighbourhood team. Officers say they are carrying out high-visibility traffic operations, speed enforcement and action against inconsiderate motorists alongside wider work tackling antisocial behaviour and organised crime in the area.

Residents say the issue extends beyond noise. High-speed driving can intimidate pedestrians, discourage people from walking to local businesses and increase the risk of collisions. Milkstone Road is a busy mixed-use corridor where children, elderly residents and shoppers regularly cross the road throughout the day.

National road safety experts have consistently warned that excessive speed dramatically reduces the time available for drivers to react while increasing both the likelihood and severity of collisions. Even where no crash occurs, repeated antisocial driving can have a lasting impact on neighbourhoods through noise, fear and disruption.

Many local residents are now calling for additional measures, including increased police patrols during evening hours, more targeted traffic enforcement, mobile speed checks and continued action against drivers found to be driving dangerously or inconsiderately.

Greater Manchester Police encourages anyone witnessing dangerous driving to report it where it is safe to do so. Dashcam footage, CCTV and details such as registration numbers, locations and times can all assist officers in identifying offenders. Residents should always call 999 if they believe there is an immediate danger to life or serious risk to road users.

For most drivers, Milkstone Road is simply another journey home or to work. However, residents hope that continued enforcement and responsible driving will ensure the road remains safe for everyone who lives, works and travels through one of Rochdale's busiest neighbourhoods.
